_comment: Notes emitted as comments above a labelled address by tools/disasm_all.py. Key: 'BB:AAAA' (hex bank, CPU address). Each note states what the instructions do and its evidence level. 'static reading' = read from the instructions only, not confirmed by running the game. Notes ending '(C1, E-0357)' were written by hand after reading the whole routine: the mechanics are a static reading, and what the routine is for (the scene, menu or state it serves, taken from its messages, flags and callers) is a C1 hypothesis.
00:0000: The rst $00 dispatcher behind the jumptable macro (507 uses in src/): pops the return address as the base of the dw list that follows the rst, adds 2 * A as a 16-bit offset (so all 256 values of A index the list), keeps DE, and falls into JumpToWordAtHL, which jumps to that entry with HL = the entry address and A = its low byte. There is no range check: an A past the end of the list reads whatever bytes follow. The dfar JumpTable entries of MonsterAttributeMapTable are zero pointers (no attribute map), not uses. (C1, E-0373)
00:0010: The rst $10 far call behind the farcall and farcall_b macros (B = ROM bank, HL = routine). Saves the number of the mapped switchable bank (read from BANK_NUMBER_BYTE, $4000), maps bank B, calls HL through JumpToHL, then maps the saved bank again. BC, DE and HL come back as the callee left them, but A and the flags do not: pop af returns A = the saved bank number and the flags as they were on entry. $10 zero bytes pad to $0030. (C1, E-0373)
00:0B18: B = ROM bank, DE = source, HL = destination, C = count (0 means 256): maps bank B, copies C bytes from DE to HL, then maps the calling bank back (saved from BANK_NUMBER_BYTE). Returns DE and HL just past the bytes, C = 0, B unchanged, A = the calling bank number. 24 call sites (LoadMonsterPicture, LoadBGPaletteBufferFromBank and others). (C2, E-0373)
00:0B2B: The interface of CopyFromBank (B = ROM bank, DE = source, HL = destination, C = count, 0 means 256) with a wait for VRAM: before each byte it disables interrupts and waits until rSTAT bit 1 is clear (mode 0 or 1, when VRAM can be written), stores the byte, then re-enables interrupts. Maps the calling bank back. 232 call sites (OpenTextChoice_DrawWindow, CopyMonsterNameToBuffer_B01 and others). (C1, E-0373)
00:0B46: B = ROM bank, DE = source, HL = destination, C = count (0 means 256): maps bank B; for each byte it waits for rSTAT bit 1 clear with interrupts off and reads [DE], then waits again and ORs the byte into [HL], advancing both; maps the calling bank back. B is clobbered (it ends as the last byte read). 17 call sites (DrawNameGlyphBufGlyphsOverlaying8DAnd8E, HibernateMenu_DrawSleeperPage_FifthNameGlyphs and others). (C1, E-0373)
00:0C5A: B = ROM bank, DE = compressed stream, HL = destination: waits while hDecompressLock is non-zero (with no time limit), sets it to 1, runs DecompressToRAM (which maps bank B and maps the calling bank back), then clears it. 34 call sites (SGBTransferCompressed, GameMode5_Init_AfterLinkBattle and others). (C2, E-0373)
00:0C69: Expands the compressed stream at DE in ROM bank B into memory at HL with plain stores (a RAM destination), then maps the calling bank back. After the header (DecompressReadHeader: size, marker) every byte other than the marker is stored as it is; the marker is followed by a position byte and a count byte: the length is the count low nibble + 4, or the next byte + $13 when that nibble is $F, and the source is the destination start + (count high nibble << 8 | position). A source at or past the destination end moves back $1000, and one then before the destination start reads as 0; an overlapping copy repeats bytes just written. It stops once the header size has been written. Only DecompressToRAMLocked calls it. Earlier reading (E-0016): 141 emulated calls matched tools/lzss_gfx.py byte for byte. (C2, E-0373)
00:0CF5: The same expansion as DecompressToRAM (format there) for destinations that may be VRAM: it spins while hDecompressLock is non-zero and then takes it, waits for rSTAT bit 1 to clear with interrupts disabled before every store (re-enabling them after), reads back-references from the destination itself, and on return maps the calling bank back and clears hDecompressLock. Callers also use it for WRAM buffers (LoadMapScreen expands into wScreenTileBuffer and wScreenAttrBuffer). (C1, E-0373)
00:0DA8: Maps ROM bank B and reads the 3-byte header of the compressed stream at DE: BC = the output size (low byte first) and hDecompressMarker = the marker byte, leaving DE past the header. Stores the destination start HL in hDecompressDestLo/Hi and in hDecompressHeader3/4, and the destination end HL + size in hDecompressHeader1/2; HL is kept. Shared start of DecompressToRAM and DecompressToVRAM, which save the calling bank first. (C2, E-0373)
00:0B6C: HL = address in the ROM bank held in wDataBank: maps that bank, reads B = [HL] and C = [HL + 1] (the first byte goes to B), leaves HL unchanged and maps the calling bank back; A = the calling bank number. 31 call sites (CopyMonsterNameToBuffer_B01, DrawKeyListPageNames, ScriptFetchMessageByScreen and others). (C2, E-0373)
00:3354: A = sound id: starts it and returns A + 1 with BC, DE and HL kept. It stores A in wSoundId, walks SoundBankTable to the range holding it (ranges start at ids 0, $1C, $31 and $A8, banks $40-$43), maps that bank and reads the 4-byte record at the range array + 4 * (id - first id): a slot offset into wSoundChannelSlots, a flags byte and the track pointer. If the slot is in use (byte 0 not $FF), the low two bits of its byte 1 pick the stereo bits of wSoundEngineMode to clear ($EE, $DD, $BB or $77). The 32-byte slot then gets 0, 0, the flags, the track pointer, the bank, $FF at byte 10 and zeros at bytes 21 and 25-31, and the ROM bank is restored. An earlier emulation of 495 sound starts agreed with this reading. (C2, E-0373)
00:33E8: The sound engine's frame step (from VBlankHandler; E-0018 identified it from its sound register writes): saves the ROM bank, starts at channel wSoundEngineState, clears wSoundSkipMaskA, counts the frame in wSoundTickBuf and goes on with the per-slot pass from wSoundChannelSlots. (C1, E-0357)
00:35CD: Fetches the next 2-byte event of the current channel: the address is hTrackBaseLo/Hi + 2 * hTrackPosLo/Hi, and the position is incremented before the event runs. Bytes $00-$9F are notes: the second byte gives hSndWaitTicks (less hSndEnvFlags low nibble when its high nibble is set); a semitone of $0C or more (noise channel: $1F) is a rest, otherwise the period comes from SoundNotePeriodTable (second row when hSndDutyAndTempo bit 4 is set) shifted right by the octave nibble and subtracted from $0800, or for a noise byte below $10 from the table at $38A0 (other noise bytes are used as they are), and it falls into ComputeNotePitch. $A0-$AF set channel values (envelope, sweep or wave, duty, note length, panning, rNR50, wave set, branch index, envelope timer, tuning, tempo, and the loop $AC and return $AD, which move the position first) and go on to the next event, except $A7, which sets the wait and ends the fetch; $B0-$BF jump to or repeat from a label slot (SoundLabelSlot), $C0-$CF set vibrato, $D0-$EF set the slide, $FD saves the position in a label slot and $FF ends the track (position $FFFF; wSoundWaveReload is set when slot 0 or 1 plays the wave channel; SoundNextEvent_MuteChannel clears its stereo bits). An earlier emulation of 5,154 fetches agreed with the address rule. (C1, E-0373)
00:3554: Starts a channel whose track position is 0 (jumped to from SoundTick_ChannelPass): reads the 4-byte track header at hTrackBaseLo/Hi. Byte 0 low nibble goes to hSndTickAccum and the tempo nibble of hSndDutyAndTempo; byte 1 gives the duty bits (bits 0-1 to 6-7), or hSndVibratoDelay on the wave channel (wSoundHwChannel = 2); byte 2, nibbles swapped, goes to hSndEnvelope; byte 3 goes to hSndSweepOrWave. On the wave channel it clears rNR30, takes byte 3 as the wave number only when hSndSweepOrWave is $FF, stores it in wSoundEventArg and copies that wave (SoundWaveSetTable set chosen by hSndWaveParam) to $FF30-$FF3F. Then it clears hSndChanUnused, hSndBranchIndex, hSndVibratoDepth, hSndPitchSlide and hTrackPosHi, sets hSndPanning = $FF and hTrackPosLo = 2 (the first event after the header) and jumps to SoundTick_NextNote. (C1, E-0373)
00:3938: HL = the frequency register value of a note (from SoundNextEvent): clears hSndVibratoCounter and returns to the caller of its caller when ReturnTwiceIfSoundSkipMaskAAndSoundSkipMaskB says the channel is skipped. On the wave channel it loads the wave pattern if it changed and sets rNR30 = $80. It writes the volume (ComputeNotePitch_WriteNR32), the sweep hSndSweepOrWave on channel 1, and L to register + $13, keeping L clamped to $02-$FD in hSndFreqLo. Channels 1 and 2 also get the duty bits with length $3F in register + $11; then the high byte (H & 7, bit 7 restarts the note except on a wave channel that is still playing) goes to register + $14 and hSndFreqHi, and the stereo bits are set from hSndPanning (ComputeNotePitch_ApplyPanning). (C1, E-0373)
00:3DAE: B = label number: returns HL = wSoundLabelSlots + wSoundChannelIndex * 12 + (B & $0F) * 3, the 3-byte label slot (a repeat counter and a saved track position) used by the track events $FD (save the position), $B0 (jump to it) and $B1-$BF (repeat). B ends as B & $0F and C as the channel * 12. The 12 bytes per channel hold 4 slots, so numbers 4-15 reach the slots of later channels. (C2, E-0373)
1B:5352: Zeroes $6F bytes from wScreenState, decompresses LetterFrameIconDigitTiles from ROM bank $46 to vTiles1, far-calls ClearScreenBufferAndAttributes_BankF1, calls LoadPalette0FromData_3, zeroes hScrollX and hScrollY, starts a palette fade (A = $FC), sets wTextWindowState = 1, wTextWindowStep = 0 and hSpriteWindowClipMode = 2, and runs StepTextWindowOpenClose until the low two bits of wTextWindowState are clear. It then requests tile fills with FillTilesRequest (HL = vTiles1, DE = $1202), sets hSpriteWindowClipMode = 2 and wLCDCShadow = 3, and ends by jumping to ResumeAfterModeChange with A = 1. No call, jump or pointer to it was found in src/. (C1, E-0379)

00:015A: Power-on start-up, then the main loop. Start-up: masks interrupts, clears WRAM, HRAM and SRAM banks 0 and 2, installs the OAM DMA routine, clears the tile area (and on CGB the BG map attributes in VRAM bank 1), selects game mode 5 (the title screen) and maps ROM and SRAM bank defaults. On CGB it loads palette 0; otherwise DetectSGB, and on a Super Game Boy it sends the start-up packet sets, transfers the border tiles and map, and sets the palettes. Every mode then starts here: clear the screen, sprites, scroll and fade, run the mode's start-up routine (RunGameModeInit), reset the frame counters. The loop halts until each interrupt (advancing the random table with NextTableByte when not linked); the per-frame work runs in VBlankHandler. When wModeChangeRequest is set and no fade is in progress (wFadeState 0 or bit 7 set), it masks interrupts, sends SGB packet set 0 and restarts at the screen clear for the new mode. (C1, E-0357)
